name: German Studies (MA)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Master's Degree: This program is designed for those who do not intend to continue their studies through the PhD degree at Stanford. To complete the MA degree, students must complete a minimum of 45 units of graduate work. If students enroll for three quarters for a minimum of 15 units per quarter, they can fulfill the MA requirements in one year.
Coterminal Master's Degree: Students may apply to combine programs for the BA and MA degrees in German Studies. Coterminal students in German Studies may count eligible courses taken up to one academic year before enrollment in the first graduate quarter. Students are reminded that course transfer is subject to the approval of the undergraduate and graduate departments.

rules.name: Remaining courses and MA oral examination

children.name: Remaining courses: approved courses in related fields (art history, comparative literature, linguistics, history, philosophy)
MA oral examination on a 45-text reading list

rules.desc:
The MA program requires students to take the three graduate core courses (GERMAN330, GERMAN331, and GERMAN332). These courses cover texts from our core reading lists in three areas of German Studies: pre-1700. 1700-1900, and post-1900. The student may select the remaining courses, but they must be graduate-level courses in German and/or approved courses in related fields such as art history, comparative literature, linguistics, history, or philosophy.
MA candidates must take an oral examination toward the end of their last quarter. In preparation for the oral exam, students are expected to compile a reading list of 45 texts comprised of:

• Ten items from each of the three core lists (pre-1700, 1700-1900, 1900-2000)

• Five items from the film/opera lists

• Ten additional items of their own choice
This MA reading list must be compiled in consultation with the advisor.

policies: See Graduate Degrees for university requirements for the master’s degree.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 45 graduate units and the three core courses, GERMAN 330, 331 and 332. The rest of the 45 units must be graduate-level GERMAN courses (numbered 200 or above) or approved courses in related fields such as art history, comparative literature, linguistics, history or philosophy; you add approved related-field courses by hand. The oral examination on your 45-text reading list is checked by hand.
